niche: a German regional newspaper group with four titles deciding which of its 2027 paid digital-subscription acquisition lines (title by channel: paid social, paid search, cashback partners, outbound telemarketing, app-store campaigns) to fund, each line against 3.5 times its planned cost per start in expected 36-month net revenue, where the 2027 lines run new introductory offers, a list-price rise lands in April 2027, the newest social and partner starts read far less than earlier ones while search starts read more, and lapsed readers come back under new customer accounts
answer: fund 8 of the plan's 18 lines (APP-BHR, PART-GAZ, SEA-BHR, SEA-ELN, SEA-GAZ, SEA-KBO, TEL-BHR, TEL-KBO) for a budget of EUR 84,308, each at least 3.5 times its planned cost per start over 36 months; not the 14 lines for EUR 141,575 the careful but hurried reading funds
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst cleans every export, models the end-of-intro exits across offers and channels, then completes each line's young starts on its older starts' survival (the newest social and partner starts look the same in their first months and read far less in the reading log), prices the April 2027 rise at the 2025 rise's after-the-date excess pooled over tenure (missing the exits filed on the notice letters and the newer subscribers' larger response), and counts later subscriptions only on the same customer number, so several lines' 36-month value per euro moves across the budget's cut and the funded list differs from the golden in several lines.
domain_test: Every result is a subscription retention quantity the cohort and lifetime-value task type estimates (the end-of-introductory-price exit by offer and channel, its response to the full price, a rise's excess cancellations over its notice window, young cohorts' survival completed from a usage covariate, later subscriptions by the same household, the 36-month net revenue per start), carried to a budget ranking; swap in a hospital or a utility and the introductory price step, the paywall's reading habit, the notice right on a price rise and the lapsed reader who re-registers stop making sense.

stakeholder_role: the head of controlling, who sets the 2027 acquisition budget's funded lines for the management board

world.org_type: a regional newspaper group with four daily titles and digital subscriptions

driver: Each candidate's value per unit of cost is the payment stream of its future entrants, whose first large drop sits at a price step set by the candidate's own terms and the full price it steps to, whose later decline follows a usage trait the newest entrants carry differently from the record (seen only in a second log at another grain, never in their early survival), which a scheduled price change cuts again at a size read only from an earlier change's whole window and the entrants' tenure at it, and which continues through returns recorded under other identities, so a ranking under a fixed budget on each candidate's own history funds a different set.
driver_concrete: Each 2027 acquisition line's expected 36-month net revenue per start, set by its 2027 introductory offer and the April 2027 list price at the step-up, the usage its newest starts show in the reading log (social and partner down since late 2025, search up since spring 2025), the April 2027 rise's excess cancellations read from the April 2025 rise including the notice-letter exits and the larger response of first-year subscribers, and later subscriptions by the same household under new customer numbers, ranked per euro of planned spend until the budget is spent.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst completes each line's newest starts on its older starts' survival, reads the April 2025 jump in end-of-intro exits as a period rather than as the full price, reads the 2025 rise's cancellations from April on pooled over tenure and counts later subscriptions on the customer number, so the four paid social lines and two cashback lines clear 3.5 times their cost and the plan funds 14 lines for EUR 141,575 instead of 8 for EUR 84,308.
results: R1 paying subscribers by title at 31 Oct 2026; R2 realised 36-month net revenue per start of the Jul-Sep 2023 starts by channel, household returns included; R3 end-of-intro exit share per 2027 offer at 2026 prices; R4 the points the April 2027 prices add; R5 two-year survival of the Nov 2025-Apr 2026 starts by channel; R6 extra cancellations from the April 2027 rise among the Oct 2026 base by title; R7 expected 36-month net revenue per start for every 2027 line; R8 the funded lines and their budget; R9 the Oct 2026 intro subscribers paying full price at Dec 2027 by title
one_fact_test: the April 2025 rise also raised the share leaving at the end of the introductory price; rescues 2 of 9 (R3, R4); no hint rescues the funded set

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-09: the project lead's review returned the single-deep-step design (one constructed factor, the tutors' stopping hump, placed in the forward cohort by an onboarding pause and surge; every graded figure came out of one projection)
lineage.driver: A unit's chance of reaching a milestone is set largely by whether the provider it is attached to keeps operating, providers stop at a rate that peaks a few months into their own tenure, and the forward group was attached almost wholly to providers in their first months, so an exit curve by the unit's own tenure, which validates on closed groups, overstates how many reach the milestone.
lineage.stump: A competent solver projects the autumn campaign's members on the platform's paid-retention curve by membership month, validated on the spring 2025 campaign and last autumn's joiners, and files about EUR 725 per twelfth-month member, inside the EUR 800 bar, and books the re-run; the step that lands it there is projecting each member on their own tenure when the member's cancellation rides on their tutor, and the autumn members' tutors are about to cross the months in which new tutors stop teaching.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-10: the platform's holistic audit failed the uploaded cut on determinism; repaired (judge DETERMINISTIC APPROVE) but the uploaded run's own methods land the repaired commitment (66.5 of 93 graded weight), the single-total risk: one cut of one total cannot be both forced and hard
lineage.driver: A forward total is the sum of several flows each set by its own mechanism (a step change still applying unit by unit at each unit's anniversary, a one-off shock whose excess exit rate has decayed on a cohort whose exits also run with the calendar, a size adjustment at each anniversary set by how much of its capacity each unit uses on a book whose capacity per user has drifted, a pipeline whose conversion falls with each item's age, and exits that arrive together within groups), so every trailing extrapolation and the recent pooled rates overstate the forward total, and the committed figure is the largest step a filed band, carrying the estimates' own sampling error and nothing else, meets at a stated chance.
lineage.stump: A careful but hurried analyst rebuilds the October 2026 ARR correctly, then applies the mean realised uplift to the contracts still to reprice, pools renewal exit and seat-cut rates without utilisation, first renewals or group exits, carries the Team plan's last three months' exit rates, values the open pipeline at the CRM's stage probabilities and draws accounts independently for the band, and files a commitment above the draft, clearing it, when large contracts negotiate the rise down, seat cuts and exits follow utilisation on a book sold more seats per user each year, the autumn is the Team plan's cancellation peak and the January excess has faded, old open deals rarely close and parent groups leave together, so the commitment sits below the draft; and a ten-minute trailing extrapolation clears the draft by a wide margin because the trailing year carries the price rise and the padded seats as if they recurred.
